Ana (oncall): multiple GPU attaches stuck in us-west2, pods at Attaching for >2m, kubelet showing block device busy :grimacing:
Carter (storage): quick check shows a scrub/sweep spike on a subset of hosts labelled `scratch-hot`. lots of small-file deletions and synchronous TRIMs at 02:20
Min (sre): did we run any maintenance that could shift cleaner timing? even small changes can collide with scale-up waves
Ana (oncall): we bumped the cleaner window by 3m to avoid a kernel rollout earlier today, might have nudged it into a provisioning wave
ops-bot: recommended mitigation: pause scrub on `scratch-hot` nodes for 10m and increase nodepool ioQuota to 1.8x
Carter (storage): pattern: burst TRIMs -> writeback stalls -> nvme qdepth collapse -> attach timeouts. sample log:
```
[2026-04-09T02:20:03Z] cleaner: trim 25k extents sync
[2026-04-09T02:20:04Z] nvme0n1: qdepth->1, avg_io_wait=240ms
[2026-04-09T02:20:05Z] kubelet: attach timeout pod=gpu-batch-9
```
Min (sre): pausing cleaner now and bumping ioQuota on `us-west2-gpu-high` pool. also add a guard so cleaner checks `attach_pending` before starting bursts
Ana (oncall): pause applied, ioQuota patched. monitoring
metrics-bot: host-local-io-latency p50 rose 2ms->140ms at 02:20; attach_pending peaked 22
Carter (storage): long-term: 1) make trims async and batched 2) add attach-aware safe-mode 3) add a low-overhead delay when qdepth<8
Min (sre): filing INF-2026-TRIM-CLASH: runbook + cleaner feature flag to avoid provisioning windows. backlog cleared after pause+quota. keeping 20m watch :thumbsup:
